artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for the Operator.aliases Unicode operator character mechanism: attribute, collection registration, error handling, seven-theory adoption, docs, and full regression.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added an optional Operator.aliases class attribute registered by OperatorCollection.add_operator alongside the canonical LaTeX name, with a conflict-aware DuplicateOperatorError policy and UnknownOperatorError on lookup; adopted curated Unicode aliases across all seven shipped theory operators.py files (discovering and fixing an alias-inheritance collision in counterfactual/candidates.py and imposition's LogosCounterfactual along the way); updated docs/usage/OPERATORS.md and five other docs that asserted the now-false 'never use Unicode' rule. Full test suite green (2834 passed in code/src/model_checker/, 647 passed in code/tests/), with dev_cli.py acceptance runs confirming identical model output for LaTeX- and Unicode-spelled formulas.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a multi-key registration mechanism (e.g. operator aliases) to a registry whose add() is called once per existing key by a deserializer, a blanket 'raise on duplicate' policy breaks the round-trip: the same class gets re-registered N+1 times. The correct policy is conflict-aware -- re-registering the SAME object under a key it already owns is a silent no-op, while a DIFFERENT object claiming a taken key raises. In ModelChecker this applies to OperatorCollection.add_operator, whose re-add paths are builder/serialize.py::deserialize_operators (iterates every dictionary key) and add_operator's own OperatorCollection-merge branch.

A subclass that does not override a non-empty class-level list attribute inherits the PARENT's actual list value via ordinary Python attribute lookup (not the base class's empty default several levels up). This is a distinct trap from the classic 'mutable default shared across siblings' bug: here the parent legitimately owns a non-empty list, and a grandchild/sibling subclass built for a genuinely different purpose (a differently-named experimental/candidate variant) silently inherits it unless it explicitly re-declares the attribute (even as an empty list) to shadow the parent's value. In ModelChecker this bit Operator.aliases: CounterfactualOperator declares aliases=['□→'], and subclasses in counterfactual/candidates.py (and imposition's LogosCounterfactual) that give themselves distinct `name`s but do not override `aliases` silently inherited '□→' and collided with it and each other once more than one was registered in the same collection. Fix: an explicit `aliases: List[str] = []` override on the shared intermediate base class (or on each leaf subclass) that never intends to share the parent's alias.
